The redirect conditions match the note. The non-owner dead end is finding 0.
I did not open the timeout and renewal code in client-runtime, so I cannot confirm the roughly 40s worst case.
verdicts.missing: packages/client-runtime/src/state/connectMcpApproval.ts and environmentHttpAuth.ts were not opened. I cannot tell whether the first authorizeDpopHttp sits outside the 10s timeout, or whether the session id survives token renewal (finding 2).

verdicts.summary: I did not open the client redirect filter, so I cannot confirm it matches the server's redirect rules.
verdicts.missing: ConnectAgentSurface.logic.ts agentRedirectUrl and McpOAuth.parseRedirect were not opened, so I cannot compare their accepted URLs.

verdicts.summary: I did not open the arming timer code, so I cannot confirm the cleanup claims.
The open question about the server-side remoteClients policy is finding 6. The fallback to the code-only page is finding 7.
The mapping of every failure to the unavailable error is finding 1. The missing-csrfToken stale-credential handling is part of finding 3.

Peer-link client IDs are not blocked on the hosted page. A crafted hosted link naming a peer-link client_id reaches approval and decision with a DPoP session, and approve() accepts session decisions for peer-link clients. The server's redirect skips the hosted page for peer-link clients, but the approval and decision endpoints do not.
verdicts.missing: I did not check whether forwardedAuthorization or validateAuthorization limits peer-link clients to a certain origin. I also did not check what token a peer-link code grants once redeemed, so I cannot say whether this is exploitable.
